An oath before God must take place between the two of them, declaring that he has not dealt dishonestly with any of his neighbor's property. The owner must accept this, and the other man must pay him nothing.
But if it is stolen while in his care, he must repay its owner.
But if a wild animal eats it, he must bring it forward as evidence of the mauling, and he must not pay for it.
If someone borrows an animal from his neighbor and it is injured, dies, or is carried off while its owner is not with it, he must pay for it.
But if its owner is with it, he must not pay for it. If he is a hired worker, it will be his in place of his wages.
If someone seduces a virgin who is not betrothed and sleeps with her, he must pay her bride-price, and she must become his wife.
But if her father does not agree and is unwilling to give her to him as his wife, he must give her father silver equal to the bride-price for virgins.
You must not let a sorcerer live.
You must put to death anyone who sleeps with an animal.
Anyone who offers a sacrifice to another god besides the Lord alone must be destroyed.
You must not mistreat a foreigner or oppress him, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You must not mistreat any widow or any orphan.
If you mistreat them cruelly and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their voice.
And I will become furious and kill you with a sword, and your wives will become widows and your children orphans.
If you lend money to your poor brother who lives near you, you must not harass him or collect interest from him.
If you take your neighbor’s cloak as a pledge, you must give it back to him before the sun sets.
For this is his only covering; it is the garment that covers his nakedness. What will he sleep in? So if he cries out to me, I will hear him, for I am merciful.
You must not speak evil of God, and you must not curse the rulers of your people.
You must give the firstfruits of the threshing floors and your winepress. You must give me the firstborn of your sons.
You must do the same with your calf, your sheep, and your donkey. It must remain with its mother for seven days, but on the eighth day you must give it to me.
You must be holy people for me. You must not eat anything that a wild animal has mauled; you must throw it to the dogs.
You must not accept a false report. You must not join hands with a wrongdoer to become an unjust witness.
You must not join a crowd in doing evil. You must not join hands with a crowd to turn aside and corrupt a judgment.
And you must not favor a poor person in a lawsuit.
If you come across your enemy’s calf or donkey straying, you must bring them back and return them to him.
If you see your enemy’s donkey fallen under its load, you must not go away and leave it. Instead, you must help him lift it up.
You must not pervert a poor person’s judgment when he seeks justice.
You must keep away from every unjust judgment. You must not kill an innocent or righteous person, and you must not acquit a wicked person for a bribe.
You must not accept bribes, for bribes blind the eyes of those who can see and corrupt truthful words.
You must not oppress a foreigner, for you yourselves know how a foreigner feels, since you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You shall sow your field for six years and gather in its produce.

But in the seventh year you shall leave it alone and let it rest, so that the poor of your nation may eat from it. The wild animals shall eat what they leave. You shall do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.
You shall do your work for six days, but on the seventh day you shall rest, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and so that your female slave’s son and the foreigner may rest.
You must observe everything I have told you. You must not mention the name of any other, foreign god, nor let their names be heard from your mouths.
Three times a year you shall celebrate a festival for me.

You shall observe the Festival of Unleavened Bread and celebrate it. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of new grain, for in that month you came out of Egypt. You shall not appear before me empty-handed.

You shall also celebrate the Festival of Harvest, of the first produce of your work in your field, and the Festival of Completion at the end of the year, when you gather in the produce of your work from your field.
Three times a year every male belonging to you shall appear before the Lord your God.
When I drive out the nations before you and expand your borders, you shall not slaughter my sacrifice and offer its blood with leavened bread, nor shall the fat of my festival remain until morning.
You must bring the firstfruits of the earliest produce of your land into the house of the Lord your God. You must not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
Look, I will send my angel ahead of you to guard you on the way and bring you into the land that I have prepared for you.
Be on your guard and obey him. Do not disobey him, for he will not show you partiality, because my name is upon him.

“If you truly listen to my voice, observe everything I command you, and keep my covenant, you will be my chosen people from among all the nations, for the whole earth is mine. You will be a kingdom and a priesthood for me, and a holy nation. These are the words you are to say to the Israelites: ‘If you truly listen to my voice and do everything I tell you, I will be an enemy to your enemies and oppose those who oppose you.’”
For my angel will go ahead of you and bring you to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, and he will wipe them out.
You shall not worship their gods or serve them, nor shall you follow their practices. Instead, you shall utterly destroy them and completely smash their pillars.
You shall serve the Lord your God, and I will bless your bread and your water and rid you of every illness.
There shall be no one childless or barren in your land. I will bring the full number of your days to completion.
I will send terror ahead of you and scatter all the nations among whom you enter, and I will make all your enemies flee before you.
I will send hornets ahead of you, and they will drive out the Canaanites, the Amorites, and the Hittites before you.
I will not drive them out in a single year, so that the land does not become desolate and the wild animals of the land do not multiply against you.
I will drive them out before you little by little, until you increase and inherit the land.

I will set your borders from the Red Sea to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the great river, the Euphrates River. I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hands and drive them out before you.
You shall not join with them, and you shall not establish a covenant with their gods.
They must not live with you in your land, so that they do not make you sin against me. For if you serve their gods, these will become a snare for you.
The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to the Lord, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, and let them worship the Lord from a distance.”
Moses alone shall approach God. They shall not approach, and the people shall not come up with them.
Moses went in and told the people all the words of God and his ordinances. All the people answered with one voice, saying, “We will do everything that the Lord has said, and we will obey it.”
Moses wrote down all the Lord’s words. He rose early in the morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, along with twelve stones for the twelve tribes of Israel.
He sent the young men of the Israelites, and they offered burnt offerings and slaughtered young cattle as offerings of well-being to God.
Moses took half of the blood and poured it into bowls, and he poured the other half of the blood at the foot of the altar.
And he took the book of the covenant and read it aloud for the people to hear. They answered, “Everything the Lord has said, we will do, and we will obey it.”
Moses took the blood and sprinkled it over the people. He said, “This is the blood of the covenant that God has established with you concerning all these words.”
Then Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel.
They saw the place where the God of Israel stood. The place beneath his feet was like a pavement of sapphire bricks, and like the appearance of the vault of heaven in its purity.
None of the chosen men of Israel uttered a sound. They appeared in the place of God, and they ate and drank.
The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain and stay there. I will give you stone tablets, the law and the commandments that I have written to establish them for you.”
Moses rose with Joshua, his attendant, and they went up to the mountain of God.
And they said to the elders, “Stay here until we return to you. Look, Aaron and Hur are with you. If anyone has a dispute, let them go to them.”
Moses went up the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
The glory of God came down upon Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day the Lord called to Moses from within the cloud.
The appearance of the Lord’s glory was like a blazing fire on the summit of the mountain in the sight of the Israelites.
Moses entered the middle of the cloud and went up onto the mountain. He remained there on the mountain for forty days and forty nights.
See that you make everything according to the pattern that you were shown on the mountain.
The two corners are equal to one another.
There shall be eight posts and sixteen silver bases for them: two bases for each one, for its two sides, and two bases for each one, for its two sides.
You shall make crossbars from wood that does not rot: five crossbars for the posts on one side of the tent,
and another five crossbars for the posts at the back side of the tent, on the seaward side, to the west.
The middle crossbar shall pass through the posts from one end to the other.
You shall cover the posts with pure gold, and you shall make their rings of gold, through which you will insert the crossbars. You shall also cover the crossbars with gold.
And you shall erect the tent according to the pattern that you were shown on the mountain.
You shall also make a curtain from blue, purple, and finely spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen, with embroidered work. You shall fashion it with cherubim.
You shall hang it on four posts of wood that does not rot, covered with gold. Their capitals shall be gold, and their four bases shall be silver.
You shall place the curtain on the posts and bring the ark of the testimony inside the curtain. The curtain shall separate for you the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
Cover the ark of the testimony with the curtain in the Holy of Holies.
Set up the table outside the curtain, and place the lampstand opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle. The table is to be placed on the north side of the tabernacle.
You shall make a covering of blue cloth.
testimony, outside the curtain that is over the covenant; Aaron shall keep it burning.
and Nadab [?], Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, who are Aaron’s sons.
And you shall make a holy garment for Aaron.
blue yarn, purple yarn, twisted scarlet yarn, and twisted fine linen.

These are the rites you shall perform for them to purify them so that they may serve me: take one bull from the herd and two rams without any defect.
And unleavened bread mixed with oil, and unleavened cakes mixed with oil. You shall make these with fine wheat flour.
Put them in one basket and bring them in the basket, together with the bull and the two rams.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of testimony, and immerse them, or wash them with water, and finish.
Take the garments and put them on Aaron your brother, including the multicolored robe, the ephod, and the breastpiece. Fasten the breastpiece to the ephod.
Put the turban on his head, and place the plate, or gold plaque of purification, on the turban.
Take some of the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
And his other sons: have them stand up and put their garments on them.
Tie their sashes around them and put headdresses on them, so that this may be for me and they may serve me forever.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Command the Israelites, saying, ‘Be careful to keep my Sabbaths, for this is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am the Lord who makes you holy.’
You must observe my Sabbaths, for the Sabbath is holy to the Lord and to you. Whoever profanes it must be put to death. Whoever does work on it, that person must be cut off from among his people.
You shall do your work for six days, but the seventh day is the Sabbath, the holy rest of the Lord. Anyone who works on the seventh day shall certainly be put to death.
And the Israelites shall keep my Sabbaths, observing them throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.
Between me and the Israelites these are a sign forever, because in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested.
When he had finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets written with the finger of God.

When the people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain, they rose up against Aaron and said to him, “Get up and make us gods who will go before us. For this man Moses, who brought us out of the land of Egypt—we do not know what has happened to him.”
Aaron said to them, “Take off the gold earrings that are in the ears of your wives and your daughters, and bring them to me.”
All the people removed the gold earrings that were in the ears of their wives and daughters and brought them to Aaron.
He took them and shaped them in a mold, and made it into a cast image. He said, ‘These are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.’
When Aaron saw it, he built an altar in front of it. Aaron made a proclamation, saying, “Tomorrow is a festival of the Lord.”
He rose early in the morning, offered burnt offerings, and made a sacrifice for well-being. The people sat down to eat and drink, and they got up to play.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying, “Leave this place quickly and go down, for your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, have acted lawlessly.”

They have quickly turned aside from the way you commanded them to follow. They have made themselves a calf and worshiped it, saying, ‘These are your gods, Israel, who brought us up from the land of Egypt.’
Now, then, leave me alone so that I may become furious with them in my wrath and wipe them out. I will make you into a great nation.
Moses pleaded before the Lord God, saying, “Why, Lord, are you angry with your people in your wrath, those whom you brought out of the land of Egypt by your great power and your uplifted arm?”

Otherwise the Egyptians might say, “He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them off the earth.” Turn away from your fierce anger, and relent from bringing disaster on your people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, your servants, to whom you swore by your own self, saying, “I will greatly multiply your descendants, making them as numerous as the stars of heaven,” and all this land, which you said you would give to their descendants, and that they would possess it forever.
The Lord relented from the disaster he had said he would bring upon his people.
Moses turned and came down from the mountain, with the two tablets of the testimony in his hands. They were stone tablets inscribed on both sides, on this side and that.
The tablets were God's work, and the writing was God's writing, engraved on the tablets.
Joshua heard the sound of the people shouting and said to Moses, “There is a sound of war in the camp.”
He said, “It is not the sound of people shouting in victory, nor is it the sound of people shouting in defeat. Rather, I hear the sound of people shouting under the influence of wine.”
When he came near the camp, he saw the calf and the dancing. Moses became furious, threw the two tablets from his hands, and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
He took the calf they had made, burned it in a fire, and ground it into powder. He scattered it over the water and made the Israelites drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, “What did these people do to you, that you brought such a great sin upon them?”
Aaron said to Moses, “Do not be angry with me, my lord. You know how impulsive these people are.
They said to me, ‘Make us gods who will go ahead of us. As for this man Moses, who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.’
I said to them, ‘Let those who have gold take it off.’ They took it off and gave it to me. I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out.”
Moses saw that the people had scattered, for Aaron had scattered them, causing their enemies to rejoice over them.
Moses stood at the gate of the camp and said, “Whoever loves the Lord, let him come to me.” All the sons of Levi came to him.

And he said to them, ‘This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Each of you must put his sword at his side. Go back and forth through the camp, from gate to gate, and each of you must kill his brother, his neighbor, and his close relative.’
The sons of Levi did these things as Moses had told them, and three thousand people fell among the people that day.
Moses said to them, “Today you have consecrated yourselves to the Lord, each through his son or his brother, so that a blessing may be given to you.”
The next day, Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to God so that I may plead for your sin.”
Moses returned to the Lord, saying, “I beg you, Lord: this people has committed a great sin. They have made gods of gold for themselves.
Now, if you will forgive their sin, then forgive it. But if not, erase me from your book that you have written.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned before me is the one I will erase from my book.
Now go down and lead this people to the place I told you about. Look, my angel will go ahead of you. And on the day when I call them to account, I will bring their sin upon them.”
The Lord struck the people because of the making of the calf that Aaron had made.

The Lord said to Moses, “Leave this place and go up, you and your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, to the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’
I will send my angel ahead of you, and he will drive out the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Hivites, Jebusites, and Canaanites,
so that I may bring you into a land flowing with milk and honey. For I will not go with you, because this people is stubborn, so that I do not destroy you along the way.”
When the people heard this harsh statement, they mourned.

The Lord said to the Israelites, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. Beware, lest I bring another plague upon you and destroy you. Now take off your splendid robes and your ornaments, and I will show you what I will do to you.’
So the Israelites took off their ornaments and their robes from Mount Horeb onward.
Moses took his tent and pitched it outside the camp, far away from the camp. It was called the Tent of Testimony.

Everyone who sought the Lord would go to the tent outside the camp. Whenever Moses went out to the tent outside the camp, all the people would stand, each at the entrance of his own tent, watching Moses as he walked until he reached the tent.
Whenever Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance of the tent, and he would speak with Moses.
All the people would see the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent. All the people would stand and worship, each at the entrance of his own tent.
The Lord spoke with Moses face to face, as someone speaks with his friend. Then he left to return to the camp. But Joshua, the servant, the son of Nun, was a young man who did not leave his tent.

Moses said to the Lord, “Look, you tell me, ‘Bring this people up,’ but you have not told me whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, ‘I know you above everyone else,’ and, ‘You have found favor with me.’

So if I have found favor in your sight, reveal yourself to me openly, so that I may see you and may continue to find favor in your sight, and so that I may know that this great nation is your people.”
He said to him, “I myself will go ahead of you and give you rest.”
And he said to him, “If you yourself will not go with us, do not bring us up from this place.
How will it truly be evident that I and your people have found favor with you, unless you go with us? Then I and your people will be honored above all the nations on earth.”
The Lord said to Moses, “I will also do this thing you have asked for, because you have found favor in my sight, and I know you above everyone else.”
And he said to him, “Show yourself to me.”

He said to him, “I will pass before you in my glory and call upon the Lord by his name in your presence. I will have mercy on whomever I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whomever I have compassion.”
He said to him, “You will not be able to see my face, for no human being can see my face and live.”
The Lord said to him, “Here is a place beside me. You must stand on the rock.”
“And when my glory passes you, I will put you in a cleft in the rock and shield you with my hand until I have passed you.”
“Then I will take my hand away from you, and you will see my back, but you will not see my face.”

The Lord said to Moses, “Cut two stone tablets for yourself like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain. I will write on the tablets my words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.”
“Be ready in the morning. Get up and come up Mount Sinai, and stand before me there on the top of the mountain.”
“Do not let anyone come up with you, and do not let anyone appear anywhere on the mountain. Do not let the sheep or cattle graze near that mountain.”
He cut two stone tablets like the first ones. Moses rose early and went up Mount Sinai, as the Lord had commanded him. Moses took the two stone tablets with him.
The Lord came down in the cloud and stood with him there, and he called upon the Lord by his name.
The Lord passed before him and called out, “The Lord, the Lord God, compassionate, merciful, patient, abundant in mercy and true,”

“preserving righteousness and mercy for a thousand generations, forgiving lawlessness, wrongdoing, and sins, but not clearing the guilty, bringing the lawlessness of the fathers upon the children and upon the children’s children, to the third and fourth generation.”
Moses quickly bowed down to the ground and worshiped,
saying, “If I have found favor in your sight, let my Lord go with us, for this people is stubborn. You will forgive our lawlessness and our sins, and we will belong to you.”

The Lord said to Moses, “Look, I will establish a covenant with you. Before all the people I will do glorious deeds that have never happened anywhere on earth or among any nation. All the people among whom you live will see the deeds of the Lord, for the things I will do for you are wonders.”
“Pay attention to what I will command you. Look, I will drive out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, Girgashites, and Jebusites.”
“Be careful not to establish a covenant with the inhabitants of the land you are entering, lest it become a snare for you in your midst.”
“You must tear down their altars, smash their pillars, cut down their sacred groves, and burn their handmade images with fire.”
“For you must not worship another god, because the name of the Lord God is Jealous; he is a jealous God.”

“Do not establish a covenant with the foreign peoples who inhabit the land, lest they prostitute themselves by following their gods and sacrifice to them, and invite you to eat from their sacrifices.”

“And lest you take their daughters for your sons and give your daughters to their sons, and your daughters prostitute themselves by following their gods and cause your sons to prostitute themselves by following their gods.”
“You must not make cast-metal gods for yourself.”

“You must observe the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days you must eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of new grain, for it was in the month of new grain that you came out of the land of Egypt.”
“Every male that opens the womb will belong to me, the firstborn of cattle and the firstborn of sheep.”

“You must exchange the firstborn of a donkey for a sheep. If you do not exchange it, you must pay its price. You must redeem every firstborn among your sons. You must not appear before me empty-handed.”
You shall work for six days, but on the seventh day you shall rest from sowing and harvesting.
You must celebrate the Festival of Weeks for me, the beginning of the wheat harvest, and the beginning of the ingathering in the middle of the year.
Three times a year every male among you shall appear before the Lord, the God of Israel.
For when I drive out the nations before you and enlarge your borders, no one shall covet your land when you go up to appear before the Lord your God three times a year.
You shall not slaughter my sacrifices so that their blood is offered with anything leavened, and the sacrifices of the Passover festival shall not be left until morning.
You must place the first produce of your land in the house of the Lord your God. You must not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
The Lord said to Moses, ‘Write down these words for yourself, for on the basis of these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.’
Moses was there before the Lord for forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water. He wrote these words on the tablets of the covenant—the ten words.
Moses came down from the mountain. Moses did not know that the appearance of the skin of his face had become radiant through his speaking with him.
Aaron and all the elders of Israel saw Moses, and the skin of his face was shining, and they were afraid to approach him.
Moses called to them, and all the leaders of the congregation returned to him, and Moses spoke with them.
After this, all the Israelites came to him, and he commanded them to do everything the Lord had told him on Mount Sinai.
